# WO-524: Scheduler: a hung or missing system tool gives a plain message, not a traceback

## Goal
The scheduler shells out to `systemctl`, `crontab`, `launchctl` and `schtasks` through `_run` (`scheduler/__init__.py:60-63`): `subprocess.run(..., text=True, timeout=60)` with the locale's text encoding. Three things go wrong on real machines: `schtasks` prints in the Windows console code page, so a non-ASCII message (Spanish or German Windows) can raise `UnicodeDecodeError`; a tool that does not answer in 60 seconds raises `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`; a tool that is missing raises `FileNotFoundError`. `install`, `remove` and `status` do not catch any of them, so the person sees a traceback. Make `_run` decode with `errors="replace"` and return a `CompletedProcess` with a non-zero return code and a short plain `stderr` for a timeout (124) and for a missing tool (127); callers already treat non-zero as failure and raise the existing plain `RuntimeError` messages. The signature and the existing messages stay.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. With `subprocess.run` monkeypatched to raise `TimeoutExpired`, `_run([...])` returns `returncode == 124` and `stderr` is a plain sentence without the command line (the command can hold paths).
2. With `FileNotFoundError`, `_run` returns 127 the same way; `status()` on a simulated linux without `systemctl` falls through to the cron branch or "not installed" as before (no exception).
3. A fake `subprocess.run` returning bytes that are not valid in the locale encoding does not raise (call the real `subprocess.run` against `sys.executable -c` printing byte 0xE9 only if `sys.executable` is allowed in the sandbox; otherwise assert that `errors="replace"` is passed to the patched `run`).
4. `install()` on each simulated platform raises the existing plain `RuntimeError` text when `_run` returns non-zero (no traceback types leak).
5. The creation-flag handling for Windows (`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`) is unchanged on win32 and still absent elsewhere (assert the kwargs passed).
6. No real process is spawned and nothing is installed; WO-334/335/350 tests and existing scheduler tests pass unchanged.
